content.text:
Mode: Planning
Needs from you: 3 decisions
Changed: 2 commits in example-repo (8332a1f source, 004c62e self-render). This finishes `proj-124`'s code. Nothing pushed.

Compliance of the previous reply: UNKNOWN. The checker can't read Cursor yet. Reading it by hand, its two claims had no "Would have falsified" or "Looked for it" fields, both of which `check_response.py:569-572` requires. They're on every claim below.

The split works, and the evidence supports it. Of the grader's roughly 730 lines, the shape rules are already self-contained. Everything else is how Copilot records a turn, built in as if it were universal. One finding also replaces my last DC1 outright: Cursor tells each command which chat it belongs to (`CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID`), so no guessing is needed.

## Your premises

P1 "you don't really do distinct response blocks, its all one long reponse where a background task can trigger more response" [factual]
- Verdict: confirmed as you experience it, with one nuance. The transcript does record separate turns: a user record, then assistant blocks, then `{"type":"turn_ended"}`. But a background notification opens a new turn that only continues the last one, and nothing in the record marks it as different apart from its fixed wording.
- Evidence for: lines 65, 91, 110, 172 and 184 of this session's transcript are all exactly `<user_query>Briefly inform the user about the task result and perform any follow-up actions (if needed).</user_query>`. The `<system_notification>` wrapper I receive is stripped before it's written.
- Evidence against: none. The separate turns are the transcript's bookkeeping, not what you see.

P2 "tool specific versions ... similar to how we do ticket.py moduels" [ruling]
- Consistent with: the "a utility is agnostic by design" prescription, and the ticket tool's pattern of one entry point with modules beside it (`tickets/tickets.py`, `edit.py`, `read.py`).
- In tension with: DC1 (a) from two turns ago, which scoped `proj-123`'s slice as a reader. This is larger, which is DC3.

## My claims

C1 The shape rules are already independent of any tool.
- Evidence for: `parse`, `check`, `grade`, `has_pointer` and the constants (`check_response.py:59-122`, `428-610`) work on plain reply text and never touch a record.
- Evidence against: `invoked_command` (`check_response.py:498-504`) sits next to them but reads a Copilot `user.message` record.
- Would have falsified: any record or transcript access inside `parse`, `check` or `grade`.
- Looked for it: yes. I read all three in full this turn.

C2 Everything else is Copilot-specific.
- Evidence for:
  - the transcript location under `Code/User/workspaceStorage` (`check_response.py:128-136`)
  - the record types `user.message`, `assistant.message` and `tool.execution_start` (`check_response.py:204-219`, `314-326`)
  - joining text by `messageId`
  - subagent pairing on `toolCallId` (`check_response.py:181-201`)
  - restarted turns keyed on `turnId == "0"` (`check_response.py:332-354`)
  - cut-short turns detected through `parentId` (`check_response.py:357-371`)
  - "delivered" meaning the output went to a terminal (`check_response.py:304-311`)
- Evidence against: none found.
- Would have falsified: any of those working unchanged on a Cursor record. None can, because Cursor records have none of those fields; the whole set is `role`, `message.content[]` and `type`/`status`.
- Looked for it: yes, by grouping all 187 transcript lines by shape this turn.

C3 Cursor has eccentricities a Copilot-shaped grader can't express.
- Evidence for:
  - Locating the session: `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID=33ff4d66-...` is set in this shell and equals this chat's transcript name. `CURSOR_AGENT=1` identifies the tool.
  - Grading in flight is impossible. The current turn isn't written until it ends: the transcript stayed at 176 lines through three tool calls, and a probe token wasn't found in it.
  - Some user records aren't turns. Line 94 is 12,054 characters of injected context (`available_subagent_types`, `dynamic_tool_catalog`) with no `<user_query>`. It falls between your message at line 93 and my reply to it.
  - Notification turns, per P1.
  - "Delivered" can't mean a terminal. Cursor's shell is never a terminal, so every run prints the "does not count" note (seen this session), and the run limit never applies.
- Evidence against: all of this comes from one session on one machine.
- Would have falsified: a second Cursor session whose turns appear in its transcript while still running, or with no context-injection records.
- Looked for it: no. One transcript was available, which is why the tests should use a fixture cut from this one.

## Logic and approach

LA1 Proposed layout, following the ticket tool's pattern:
- `responses/check_response.py`: the entry point. It picks a tool, asks it for turns, and runs the shared grading.
- `responses/shape.py`: the shape. Parse, check, grade, the exit codes, the "not checked" footer, and the look-back walk over a neutral list of turns.
- `responses/copilot.py` and `responses/cursor.py`: one adapter each, all with the same four parts:
  - `detect()`: from the environment. Cursor is checked first, because it also sets `VSCODE_*`.
  - `locate(args)`: finds this session's transcript, or refuses.
  - `turns(path)`: returns a list of turns, each carrying its kind (operator, notification or starter), its reply text, whether it ran the check, and whether it was cut short.
  - `in_flight` and `delivered`: whether the tool supports grading the reply being written, and what counts as a verdict being seen.
- `--tool` overrides detection. If detection finds both tools or neither, the script refuses with UNKNOWN rather than guessing.
- Adding OpenCode would then be one new file, and nothing in the shape code changes.

LA2 How the Cursor adapter models a turn:
- Only your messages start gradeable turns. Injected-context records are dropped.
- A notification turn is a continuation. It isn't graded and owes no recap, but it doesn't end the look-back walk, so the substantive reply before it still gets graded.
- The reply graded is the turn's last text block. The earlier blocks are progress notes between tool calls, which is how I actually post in Cursor.
- Notifications are recognised by their fixed wording. If Cursor rewords them, they get graded as normal turns and fail loudly, which is the safe direction to break.

LA3 The existing tests become characterisation tests for the Copilot adapter plus the shared code, run unchanged before and after the move. A test passing on both sides is what shows the move changed nothing. The Cursor adapter gets new tests against a trimmed fixture cut from this transcript.

## Decisions and clarifications

DC1 Where the entry point lives.
- Use case: the routing table in every repo tells agents to run `python .github/scripts/check_response.py`. Moving it changes an instruction, which has to happen in the same commit.
- Options:
  - a. A new `.github/scripts/responses/` directory, with the routing line updated in the same commit.
  - b. Keep `.github/scripts/check_response.py` as the entry point, with modules in a sibling directory.
- Recommendation: (a). It's the same shape as `tickets/`, and two homes for one tool is the kind of drift you rejected for identity.
- Would change my answer: if anything outside the rendered files calls the old path. The rollout covers every repo, so I'd only know by searching, which I'll do before building either option.

DC2 Grade the last text block of a Cursor turn, rather than all of them joined.
- Use case: it decides whether progress notes can ever produce findings.
- Options:
  - a. The last block only.
  - b. All blocks, with grading starting at the first `Mode:` line, as the Copilot path does.
- Recommendation: (a). Under (b), a progress note that happens to contain a line starting `mode:` would derail the parse.
- Would change my answer: if you want the shape to span a reply split across blocks. I don't currently write one that way.

DC3 This is bigger than `proj-123`'s Done-when ("a test covers the Cursor transcript reader"), so per the prescriptions it's a separate ticket.
- Use case: it's the difference between a slice of `proj-123` and a new piece of work that `proj-123` waits on.
- Proposal: file "check_response: shared shape core with per-tool adapters, Copilot and Cursor first" with Severity: High. The reason is that the look-back check can't run in Cursor at all. It would block `proj-123`, ship in the same rollout, and later move to `ai-toolbox` as a generic piece.
- Recommendation: file it, and build it before the `proj-126` hook renderer. It's the check every reply after it depends on.
- Would change my answer: if you'd rather the rollout not wait on it. Then it ships in a second rollout.

## Recommended next

R1 Once DC1 to DC3 are answered: search for callers of the old path, then cut the Cursor fixture from this transcript, then run the existing suite as the characterisation baseline. After that, move the code, write the Cursor adapter tests first, and build.
- Reasoning: the move has to be shown safe before anything new is added on top of it.
- Evidence: LA3.

The CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID gives an exact locator for this session, and CURSOR_AGENT=1 identifies the tool directly, so that resolves DC1 cleanly. The notification identification relies on matching a fixed string since the system_notification block gets dropped from the transcript, which feels brittle — if Cursor ever reworded that text, those turns would silently get graded as normal instead of being flagged.

Now I'm thinking through the file layout: mirror the tickets/ pattern by creating a responses/ directory with check_response.py plus supporting modules for shape, copilot, and cursor logic, rendered to .github/scripts/responses/. That changes the invocation path though, so the routing table would need updating — unless I keep a thin shim at the old path, though that introduces duplication I'd rather avoid, so I'm leaning toward just committing to the new path cleanly.

I'm also sketching the shared vs adapter split: shape.py holds core logic (parsing, checking, grading, pointer detection, constants, lookback walk over a normalized Turn list, budget/ledger, NOT CHECKED footer, exit codes), while each tool module exposes a detect/locate/turns/in_flight_supported/delivered interface — with all the Copilot-specific record-format handling (subagent filtering, restarted turns, cut_short, messageId joining) pushed into the Copilot adapter since that's where those semantics belong.

For delivery detection, Cursor can't reliably tell if stdout is piped since it's never a tty, so I'm leaning toward treating every completed run as delivered and relying on instructions to mitigate the pipe-truncation risk. For tool selection: an explicit `--tool` flag overrides, otherwise auto-detect, and if detection is ambiguous (both or neither match) it should refuse with UNKNOWN — also need to be careful that Cursor being a VS Code fork means its env vars overlap with Copilot's, so detection must check Cursor-specific markers first or rely on vars unique to each.

Now I'm mapping out Cursor's turn model: operator turns are real user queries, notification turns are continuations that don't need grading or recap, and context-injection records aren't turn boundaries at all — they just merge into the surrounding operator turn, so the reply still belongs to the preceding operator query and injection records get dropped from consideration.

For grading reply text, I'm realizing only the final text block matters since progress notes are interleaved before the shaped final message with its "Mode:" header — joining all blocks and parsing from the first "Mode:" line only works if no progress note accidentally starts with "mode:", so it's safer to just grade the last text block alone.

Separately, I'm noting that notification-style turns get skipped under the lookback cap, and the existing Copilot-fixture tests would need to move into the Copilot module while core logic stays unchanged as a characterization test. This change also looks broader than the original ticket's slice, so I need to check whether it requires a new ticket given the rule about altering exit criteria.

The ticket's done-when condition is satisfied by this refactor but adds scope — the orchestrator split. I'm leaning toward proposing a separate ticket for that split, with this ticket's criterion satisfied as a blocking dependency, and asking for approval on title/severity before deciding if it rides along with the rollout. I also want to flag that the tool modules fit naturally into the toolbox's generic/profile-toggleable pattern, and there's still an open design question about the entrypoint path.

Now shifting to structuring the actual reply: I need to include claims with evidence, falsifier, and "looked for it" fields since previous replies were missing those and got flagged. One premise to address is the user's claim that responses aren't really distinct blocks — I think the truth is nuanced: turns are distinct within the transcript structure, but appear continuous from the operator's view, so I'll confirm with that caveat and keep the whole thing concise.
